title: Rav Chiyya bar Rav, of Difti
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: For the most part we find him reciting baraitot, as in Shabbat 10a, where he taught Rav Chisda and Rabbah son of Rav Huna: “Every judge who judges a truly true judgment even for one hour,” etc.; Berakhot 8b, where he taught Rav Bivi bar Abaye: “Do they fast on the ninth?” etc.; Shabbat 142b: “And so Chiyya son of Rav of Difti taught”; Yevamot 74a: “Come and hear, for Rabbi Chiyya son of Rav of Difti taught: An uncircumcised person is forbidden,” etc.; and Ketubot 68a: “Rabbi Chanina said … and Rabbi Chiyya son of Rav of Difti taught.” Hyman argues that this does not mean that he lived in Rabbi Chanina’s time; it is the anonymous Gemara. Hyman identifies this Rabbi Chanina as not the first Rabbi Chanina, but the one described as a colleague of the Rabbis or of Rabbi Mani, for he said there “for Rabbi Elazar said.” Hyman supports this by noting that this statement he said to Rav Papa in Bava Batra 10a: “Perhaps a poor man came to you and you did not support him, for it was taught: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha says: Whoever closes his eyes to charity is as though he serves idolatry,” etc. Hyman considers it no wonder that he lived in Rav Chisda’s time and was still alive in Rav Papa’s time, for when he was before Rav Chisda, it was when Rav Chisda headed the academy, at the end of his days, and Rav Chiyya son of Rav was then young; in Rav Papa’s time he was already old.

notes.text: Bar Rav is retained as the patronymic form, with of Difti modifying Chiyya rather than asserting that Rav himself is from Difti. The reciter role, anonymous-Gemara distinction and long-life reconstruction are Hyman’s arguments. The supplied חברון דרבנן remains a general colleague description, not an invented new proper name.

Shabbat 10a directly names Chiyya bar Rav of Difti teaching Chisda and Rabbah bar Huna. It does not independently prove Hyman’s anonymous-Gemara distinction, later Chanina identification or the proposed long life spanning Chisda and Papa.
